sections.html:
Homeowners in St. Peters generally choose between an agent's listing, a do-it-yourself sale and an investor's as-is cash price. Owners live in most homes here, so an ordinary listing finds plenty of interested buyers. Cash works better for a house in need of repair or a seller with a firm deadline.

  • Agent listing: reach to buyers with loans, along with showings and repair requests once their inspector visits.
  • Selling alone: you skip the commission and take on the contract and disclosures.
  • Investor purchase: a faster timeline with no haggling over repairs, since the offer already reflects the buyer's view of the work.

The city covers 22.37 square miles northwest of St. Louis along the Interstate 70 corridor. The mid-2025 population estimate is 61,479, up 6.5% from the 2020 base. Amenities worth mentioning in a listing include a park and trail system of more than 1,000 acres, the Rec-Plex beside City Hall and Barnes-Jewish St. Peters Hospital.

With rents at $1,321, an owner weighing a sale against keeping the house as a rental has a real option to consider. Compare what the house would earn as a rental with the cash a sale would put in your hands.

None is required when the home is owner-occupied. The city's Certificate of Occupancy page states plainly that St. Peters does not require an occupancy inspection for the sale of an owner-occupied home.

Rentals are another story. The city requires a Certificate of Occupancy on any change in use, tenancy or occupancy of a non-owner-occupied single-family house or a multi-family dwelling. A re-occupancy inspection is needed each time the occupant is not the owner on file with the St. Charles County Recorder of Deeds. That covers houses, townhouses, condos, duplexes and apartments, and the inspection can reach all areas of the building.

  • Owner-occupied sale: no city occupancy inspection.
  • Rented house changing tenants: application, fee, inspection and permit.
  • Applications and payments run through the city's CitizenServe portal, with questions at 636-477-6600, extension 1670.

When a tenant is living in the house you plan to sell, ask the city whether the buyer will need a fresh occupancy permit after closing.

Three districts touch the city. The north and northwest parts are in the Fort Zumwalt School District, the southern part is in the Francis Howell School District, and a northeast sliver is in the St. Charles R-VI School District.

Three public high schools sit inside the city limits: Fort Zumwalt South, Fort Zumwalt East and Francis Howell North. Some St. Peters students attend schools in neighboring Cottleville or O'Fallon, so confirm the assigned school for your exact address with the district.

St. Peters lies in St. Charles County, and the county Recorder of Deeds handles its deeds from 201 N. Second Street in St. Charles, phone 636-949-7900. Per-page charges come from the county fee schedule, which the recorder updates, so confirm the amount before you send anything in.

If you are the one recording, such as a lien release from a lender, call the office first so the document meets the format rules. City Hall is at One St. Peters Centre Boulevard, and its main line is 636-477-6600.

sections.h2: Selling a house with a tenant
sections.html:
Because the city ties its occupancy rules to who lives in the house, a rented property needs a little more planning than an owner's home. Find out when the lease ends and what notice it requires, then tell the tenant in writing once a contract exists. Decide with the buyer whether the house will be empty or occupied at closing.

An investor may be glad to keep the tenant and take over the lease. A buyer who wants to move in will need the house vacant, which can mean negotiating a later closing date. Either way, ask the city about the occupancy permit before you sign, so the buyer is not surprised by an inspection after the sale.

Before you invite offers, write down your own numbers: the date you need to close, what the house costs you monthly in payments, tax and upkeep, and the repair list a buyer would see. A cash offer that arrives quickly looks different when you subtract the months of carrying costs a listing would add.

With owners making up most of the neighborhood buyers, a clean house in good shape can do well on the open market. A house with deferred maintenance often does better with a buyer who will take it as it is. Get one of each kind of offer if you can, and compare what you would actually keep.

The National Weather Service reported 12.3 inches of rain in St. Peters on July 26, 2022, an unofficial record. Buyers who remember that flooding may ask about the basement, sump pump and grading, so keep records of any waterproofing or drainage work you have done.

A cash buyer will price in the condition of the roof, gutters and cooling system, while a financed buyer may ask for repairs after inspection.

Your first decision is who will be living in the house at closing, because that settles whether the city's occupancy rules apply.

  • Owner-occupied: no city occupancy inspection for the sale, so focus on repairs buyers will see.
  • Rented: ask the city about the Certificate of Occupancy that applies when the occupant changes.
  • Gather records for any basement waterproofing, sump pump or drainage work, given the July 2022 rainfall.
  • Check the school district for the address, because three districts serve the city.
  • Ask the closing agent to confirm recording costs with the county recorder.

The park and trail system, with its fishing ponds, athletic fields and picnic shelters, is a selling point that holds across districts. Mention it in a listing if your house is nearby.

A cash sale goes from written offer to title search to signing to recording. A buyer with a loan inserts an appraisal and underwriting step. Whichever you face, have your deed, payoff statement and most recent tax bill ready so closing is not delayed.

faqs.q: Does selling an owner-occupied house in St. Peters trigger an occupancy inspection?
faqs.a: No. The city says it does not require an occupancy inspection for a sale as long as the property is owner occupied. Rentals changing tenants do need a Certificate of Occupancy.

faqs.q: What school district is St. Peters in?
faqs.a: Three. Fort Zumwalt has the north and northwest, Francis Howell has the south, and a northeast sliver is in St. Charles R-VI. Ask the district to confirm yours.

faqs.q: Who records a deed for a St. Peters house?
faqs.a: The St. Charles County Recorder of Deeds at 201 N. Second Street in St. Charles, reachable at 636-949-7900. The closing agent normally files it, and the fee is paid from settlement funds.

faqs.q: How high are St. Peters home values?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $269,900, and median gross rent is $1,321, based on 2020 to 2024 estimates.

faqs.q: Can a St. Peters rental house be sold with a tenant inside?
faqs.a: Yes, though a new occupant in a non-owner-occupied house brings the city's occupancy permit rules into play. Call 636-477-6600, extension 1670, to learn what the buyer will need after closing.
